p: Here's the thing about karting: one go rarely settles it. The person who came last will be demanding a rematch before the helmets are off, and the person who won will want to prove it wasn't a fluke. Before you know it, it's become a monthly fixture.

If that sounds like your crew, keep a note of your lap times and track how you're getting on. Having a personal best to beat gives every visit a point, even if you're not going to top the board. Some groups even run their own little championship, with points for finishing positions across several visits.
To make real progress, focus on the basics: smooth steering, braking in a straight line before the corner, and getting back on the power as early as you can on the way out.
Leeds station is one of the busiest in the North, with trains from across Yorkshire and beyond, so getting the whole group together is rarely a problem.

Leeds is a great city to fill out a day. Kirkstall Abbey is a beautifully preserved Cistercian ruin on the edge of the city, free to wander around. Leeds Art Gallery sits on The Headrow with the Henry Moore Institute right next door. And if you're after something a bit quirky, the Thackray Museum of Medicine is fascinating, if not for the squeamish.
